content:
Primes, divisibility tests, HCF and LCM — Playing with Numbers is the highest-yield chapter of Class 6 number theory, and a favourite for Olympiad word problems. Here is what it tests, the rules to know cold, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Playing with Numbers chapter tests

  • Factors, multiples, primes, composites, co-primes and twin primes
  • Divisibility tests for 2–11
  • Prime factorisation, HCF and LCM
  • HCF/LCM word problems (bells, rods, stacks)

Key facts your child should know

  • 1 is neither prime nor composite; 2 is the only even prime.
  • Digit sum ÷ 3 ⇒ number ÷ 3; alternating sum ⇒ test for 11.
  • HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
  • Greatest/exact-cut → HCF; together-again/smallest-common → LCM.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Calling 1 a prime.
  • Choosing HCF when the problem needs LCM (and vice-versa).
  • Missing a prime factor in the tree.

questions.q: Is 143 a prime number or a composite number?

Find the HCF of 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 and 2^2 x 3^3 x 7.
questions.explanation: HCF = minimum powers of common primes = 2^2 x 3^2 = 36.

faq.q: How do I know whether to use HCF or LCM?
faq.a: Largest piece, greatest length, exact division → HCF. Ringing together, meeting again, smallest common quantity → LCM.
Two numbers whose HCF is 1, like 8 and 15 — they need not themselves be prime.
